classification.difficultyReason: Count the supplied categories, construct separate columns and convert counts to proportions and percentages using the given sample size; these are familiar linked representations.

inlines.text: A bin contains black, blue and green marbles. A sample of 20 marbles is taken from the bin. The results are as shown:
green, black, green, blue, green, black, green, blue, black, black, green, black, black, green, green, green, black, green, green, black

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a column graph showing the frequency of each category.

answer.short: Blue: 2; green: 10; black: 8. See the column graph.
answer.worked: Counting the marbles gives 2 blue, 10 green and 8 black marbles. These frequencies total $2+10+8=20$. Draw separate columns with heights 2, 10 and 8, with colour on the horizontal axis and frequency on the vertical axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1a; answer graph on teacher PDF page 44
spec.description: Separate unfilled columns in blue, green, black category order, with frequency ticks from 0 to 12 in steps of 2 and horizontal grid lines.
spec.mathematics: Blue frequency 2, green frequency 10, black frequency 8; total 20.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the relative frequency of each category.

answer.worked:
Relative frequency is the frequency divided by the sample size, 20.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Black relative frequency}&=\frac{8}{20}=\frac25\\\text{Blue relative frequency}&=\frac{2}{20}=\frac1{10}\\\text{Green relative frequency}&=\frac{10}{20}=\frac12\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the relative frequency of each category as a percentage.
